content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually increase — suggesting a lag in capturing short-term price momentum.
- After sharp price spikes in history, forecasts overshoot and then correct — indicating a failure to account for post-spike mean reversion.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: forecasts often revert to historical averages too quickly, missing sustained trends.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window, suggesting overconfidence in upward momentum.
- Model fails to capture downward price corrections after initial spikes — underestimates volatility in the middle of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts are systematically too low when true outcomes show strong downward momentum — especially in the 10–20 day range.
- Model tends to overestimate price stability in the first 5 days, then underestimates volatility in the last 5 days.
